claim: The Task MCP dashboard ships no standalone HTTP/browser-facing server process. Dashboard data is exposed exclusively as read-only MCP tool views (aiworkhub/dashboard_mcp_app.py) consumed by the VS Code webview; there is no socket bound to a TCP port, no WSGI/ASGI app, and no browser-reachable listener anywhere in the aiworkhub package.
method: Recursive scan of every *.py file under tools/geoai-task-mcp/src/aiworkhub/ (44 files) for HTTP/WSGI/ASGI server signatures: http.server, socketserver, BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer, flask, Flask, wsgiref, uvicorn, gunicorn, app.run(, and any .bind(/.listen( call.

socket_listen_detail.classification: AF_UNIX domain socket bound to a local filesystem sideband path (self._socket_path, mode 0o600), used for VS Code app-server-mux instance coordination -- not a TCP/HTTP listener, not browser-reachable, no HTTP protocol framing

dashboard_delivery_paths: src/aiworkhub/dashboard.py -- pure read-only snapshot/detail builders (DashboardProvider, build_snapshot, build_task_detail); no server loop, no socket

src/aiworkhub/dashboard_mcp_app.py -- registers MCP tool views (snapshot_view, health_view, task_detail_view, initialize_view) returned over the existing MCP stdio transport; no HTTP route, no port bind
src/aiworkhub/dashboard_static/ -- static JS/CSS assets rendered inside the VS Code webview sandbox by the extension host, never served by this Python package over a socket

readme_cross_check: README.md `## VS Code Dashboard` section documents the dashboard as read through `aiworkhub/dashboard.py` via a repository-local Task MCP server, opened with the `AIWorkHub: Open Dashboard` VS Code command -- no browser URL, port, or standalone HTTP server is documented anywhere in README.md.
